Subject: Clarification on output ownership + no‑learn request

Marcus —

Thanks for the demo last week. Legal asked us to document two items before we can proceed to a pilot:

1) We need explicit language that any prompts we send and the model outputs generated for our account are ours (including IP in the generated artifacts), or that Redwood grants BrightHealth a worldwide, royalty‑free license to use the outputs.

2) BrightHealth requires a formal "no‑learn" commitment for pilot data: our prompts/responses cannot be used to train or improve production models (no model improvement). If you cannot prohibit learning entirely, we need an opt‑out mechanism and a technical plan for segregation/auditability.

Can you share a redline of the DPA showing those changes and a list of subprocessors that may touch inference data? Also need the KMS/region for key management for this workspace.

Sanjay

BrightHealth

Appreciate the clear ask. Short answers up front: we can (1) provide contract language that assigns output rights/licensing to BrightHealth and (2) offer a no‑learn addendum for data used during the pilot with a documented operational workflow.

Attached: a draft "no_learn_addendum_draft.docx" and our current DPA with a couple of suggested redlines (BrightHealth_DPA_redline_v1.pdf). Key points to note:

- Output ownership: We typically grant customers ownership or an express license for outputs; I'll propose a clause that makes BrightHealth the owner of generated outputs for their account for the duration of the agreement.
- No‑learn: For pilot data we can switch the workspace to a "no‑learn" mode where requests are routed to inference pools that do not feed back into model training. That includes disabled aggregator telemetry for model improvement and separate log routing.
- Subprocessors: attaching an exportable inventory (subprocessor_inventory_2025-06-18.csv). The inference path touches: our serving runtime, telemetry pipeline (disabled in no‑learn mode), cloud provider managed GPUs, and our metrics aggregator.

Priyom and Neha are looped for privacy and legal operational details. Next steps I propose: you review the addendum, we sync on the KMS/region (we support AWS KMS in us‑west‑2 and bring‑your‑own keys via customer KMS), and we schedule a short ops walkthrough.

Action items:
- Marcus: send a scoped KMS/ops note (by EOD)
- Priyom: propose precise redline language for the no‑learn/outputs clause
- Neha: confirm what telemetry we can fully suppress and provide evidence artifacts we can share

Thanks,
Marcus Lin

Folks —

Draft language suggestions below (short form). I put these into the attached redline for Marcus to forward. High level notes: keep the no‑learn scope narrow to the customer workspace(s) to avoid platform‑wide regressions, but make it auditable.

Suggested clauses:
- "Customer Generated Artifacts": Redwood hereby assigns to Customer all right, title and interest in and to Outputs generated by Redwood services in response to Customer data or prompts, subject to any third‑party model licenses and export controls.
- "No Model Improvement": For the duration of this Agreement (and any specified Pilot period), Redwood will not use Customer Data or Outputs to train, fine‑tune, or improve models that are used in its production offerings. Redwood will route Customer Data to an isolated inference cluster and disable model improvement telemetry for that cluster.
- "Audit Evidence": Redwood will provide a signed statement of cluster segregation and a daily summary log (redacted) showing that no aggregate model improvement jobs consumed the pilot workspace data.

Subprocessor notes: ensure the CSV includes subprocessor roles and whether they have access to raw text, KV caches, or only telemetry hashes. Also confirm contractual flow‑down with the cloud provider for ephemeral GPU instances.

Neha — can you enumerate the exact telemetry streams we can disable and confirm what evidence artifacts are safe to share with the customer? I want to keep the language operational but not expose internal metrics schemas.

Priyom
Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: subprocessor_inventory_2025-06-18.csv]

Thanks — we can meet the asks. Quick operational answers and attachments below:

1) BYOK/KMS: With a customer‑provided AWS KMS key (us‑west‑2), Redwood will encrypt request payloads at rest with the customer key; plaintext for inference is only present in the ephemeral GPU memory on the instance and is not persisted to model training stores. We will not feed any customer workspace data into model improvement pipelines while the workspace is in no‑learn mode. See attached diagram (data_flow_kms_diagram.png).

2) Runbook & Evidence: Attached a one‑page runbook and an evidence checklist we can sign (we will provide the daily redacted summary and a signed segregation attestation). We'll convert the redline to a PDF and produce a DocuSign package if you confirm the legal contact.

3) Outputs IP: We'll assign Outputs to BrightHealth where the outputs are wholly generated from your prompts and data. If any output is materially derived from a third‑party model license that restricts assignment, we'll provide a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty‑free license to BrightHealth.

Next steps: Marcus to upload PDF redline and runbook to DocuSign link (will post when ready). Priyom/Neha to prepare the signed attestation copy and the telemetry suppression checklist.

I'll prepare the DocuSign bundle first thing Monday unless you want it sooner.
